evidence.text: Tegra Processor Business. The gross margin of our Tegra Processor business decreased during fiscal year 2016 when compared to fiscal year 2015 due to inventory provisions, the warranty charge associated with the SHIELD 8-inch tablet product recall, and a less rich product mix resulting from higher automotive and SHIELD product sales and lower sales of OEM smartphone and tablet products. The inventory provisions related primarily to older generation Tegra products, as well as inventory purchase commitments in excess of estimated demand and excess component inventories for SHIELD products. The gross margin of our Tegra Processor business decreased during fiscal year 2015 when compared to fiscal year 2014. These decreases were driven primarily by a combination of an overall decline in margins of our Tegra products and a less rich mix between tablet products, which have had higher gross margins, and smartphone and automotive module products, which have had comparably lower gross margins.

attrs.management_says: CFO increased due to changes in working capital and higher non-cash expenses (stock-based compensation, restructuring, inventory provisions), partially offset by lower net income.
attrs.numbers_show: Net income fell $16.6M ($630.6M → $614.0M) while CFO rose $269.3M ($905.7M → $1,175.0M). Inventory provisions charged to cost of sales rose $53M ($59M → $112M). SGA increased $121.2M ($480.8M → $602.0M), consistent with higher stock-based compensation. Restructuring charges are noted. The non-cash charge increase alone accounts for a large share of the CFO/net income gap.

attrs.numbers_show: COGS rose from $2,082M to $2,199M (E2, E14); gross margin pressure consistent with higher provisions. Tegra margin decline attributed to provisions, warranty charge, and mix shift (E44).

attrs.reason: While inventory provisions rose $53M (E43) and SGA increased $121M (E3 vs E15), the pack does not disclose stock-based compensation expense, restructuring charges, or working capital changes (receivables, inventory, payables) needed to verify that these drivers are large enough to explain the $269M CFO increase alongside a $17M net income decline.
